meta.titre: Computer Generations: from vacuum tubes to microprocessors and AI
meta.sous_theme: Technology of each generation, programming languages and translators

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In a shop in Yaounde you can buy a smartphone that fits in your pocket and is faster than the room-sized machines of the early days of computing. This change happened in steps, and each step was marked by a new electronic part. The GCE asks you to name the main technology of each generation and to answer related questions on programming languages. A clear table in your head is enough to collect these marks.

items: A computer is an electronic machine that processes data using a stored program.
A program is a list of instructions that the computer carries out.
Computer circuits understand only two states, written 0 and 1.

sections.titre: Computer generations: from vacuum tubes to microprocessors and AI
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Five generations

Computers are grouped into **generations**. Each new generation began when a new electronic component made machines smaller, faster and more reliable. The dates are approximate.

| Generation | Approximate period | Main technology | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| First | 1940s to late 1950s | **Vacuum tubes** | Huge machines, much heat, frequent failures, programmed in machine language |
| Second | Late 1950s to mid 1960s | **Transistors** | Smaller, cooler, faster and more reliable; assembly language and the first high-level languages |
| Third | Mid 1960s to 1970s | **Integrated circuits** (many transistors on one small silicon chip) | Smaller, cheaper, faster; high-level languages widely used |
| Fourth | 1970s onward | **Microprocessors** (a whole CPU on one chip) | Personal computers, cheap and small, networks |
| Fifth | Present and future | **Artificial intelligence** and parallel processing | Machines that learn, reason and respond to speech |

Remember the chain: vacuum tube, transistor, integrated circuit, microprocessor.

### Programming languages

- **Machine code** is written in binary (0s and 1s) and is the only language the CPU runs directly. Its disadvantages: it is very hard to read, write and remember; errors are easy to make and hard to find; and a program for one type of CPU will not run on another type.
- **Assembly language** replaces binary with **mnemonics**: short abbreviations such as ADD or SUB that stand for instructions. An **assembler** translates it into machine code.
- **High-level languages** use English-like words and are translated by a **compiler** or an **interpreter**.

### Compiler and interpreter

A **compiler** translates the whole program into object code before it runs. The object code can then run again and again without the compiler, and all errors are reported together. An **interpreter** translates and runs the program one line at a time, stops at the first error and keeps no object code, so the program must be translated again at every run.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks about mnemonics, machine code or assemblers
variantes.contenu_markdown: Machine code is binary and machine-dependent. Assembly language uses mnemonics and needs an assembler. A high-level language is easier for people but needs a compiler or interpreter. Always say what the translator changes into what: assembler (assembly to machine code), compiler or interpreter (high-level to machine code).

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for differences
variantes.contenu_markdown: State differences in pairs. Compiler: whole program at once, produces object code, errors listed at the end, fast to re-run. Interpreter: one line at a time, no object code kept, stops at the first error, slower to re-run but good for testing small programs.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a description is given and you must name the generation
variantes.contenu_markdown: Look for the key word: bulbs or valves and heavy heat mean first generation; transistors mean second; many components on one chip mean third; a whole processor on one chip means fourth; artificial intelligence means fifth.

sections.enonce_markdown: Name the generation described in each case and give a reason. (a) A machine built with thousands of glass bulbs that heated the room and failed often. (b) A machine in which separate solid-state switches replaced the bulbs, so it was smaller and cooler. (c) A machine whose components were made together on one small silicon chip. (d) A personal computer whose whole processor sits on one chip. (e) Explain why assembly language was easier to use than machine code.

etapes.justification: Glass bulbs that produce heat and fail are vacuum tubes.
Small solid-state switches that replaced the bulbs are transistors.
Many components made together on one silicon chip form an integrated circuit.
A complete CPU on one chip is a microprocessor.
Machine code is a long string of 0s and 1s, while assembly uses short mnemonics that people can read and remember.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Assembly language uses **mnemonics** such as ADD, so programs are easier to write, read and correct; an assembler then converts them into machine code.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The generations are first (vacuum tubes), second (transistors), third (integrated circuits) and fourth (microprocessor). Assembly language is easier than machine code because mnemonics replace strings of binary digits.

items.erreur_markdown: Second generation computers used integrated circuits.
items.pourquoi_faux: Integrated circuits belong to the third generation.
Mnemonics are short letter abbreviations for instructions. The binary form is produced afterward by the assembler.
items.correction_markdown: A mnemonic such as ADD stands for an instruction; the assembler converts it to **machine code**.

items.erreur_markdown: A compiler translates one line at a time.
items.pourquoi_faux: That describes an interpreter. A compiler translates the whole program.

items.erreur_markdown: Machine code is easy to use because the computer understands it.
items.pourquoi_faux: The computer understands it, but people find long binary strings hard to read and write.
items.correction_markdown: Machine code is **difficult for programmers** and depends on the type of CPU.

items.erreur_markdown: Vacuum tubes were used in the fourth generation.
items.pourquoi_faux: Vacuum tubes belong to the first generation. The fourth uses microprocessors.

items.enonce_markdown: Put these components in the order in which they appeared: microprocessor, vacuum tube, integrated circuit, transistor.
State three advantages that second generation computers had over first generation computers.
items.solution_markdown:
Any three of the following:

- They were smaller because transistors are much smaller than vacuum tubes.
- They produced less heat.
- They were more reliable and failed less often.
- They were faster.
- They used less electrical power.

The key technology change was from vacuum tubes to **transistors**.

items.enonce_markdown: A company runs a payroll program every month in 50 branches. A teacher also tests short programs written by students during a lesson. Choose a compiler or an interpreter for each case and justify your choice.
items.solution_markdown:
**Payroll program: compiler.** The program is translated once into object code, which can be run every month in all branches without the source code and runs quickly.

**Teacher's tests: interpreter.** It runs the program line by line and stops at the first error, so students see exactly where the fault is and can correct and rerun quickly.

items_markdown: Generation key: first vacuum tubes, second transistors, third integrated circuits, fourth microprocessors, fifth artificial intelligence.
Each generation became smaller, faster, cheaper, cooler and more reliable.
Machine code is binary, hard for people to use and depends on the CPU type.
Mnemonics are short abbreviations for instructions in assembly language; an assembler converts them to machine code.
A compiler translates the whole program into object code; an interpreter translates and runs one line at a time.
